items.title: Intel's stock crashes, knocking $12B from government's stake
items.snippet: Intel is being hurt by PC sales as the AI industry gobbles memory and other components causing PC prices to rise.

items.title: AI law firm Crosby bids on disintegrating, famed firm Weil Gotshal

items.title: Russia Places Apple on State Surveillance Registry
items.snippet: Apple faces Russian data retention and disclosure requirements after being added to the country's state surveillance registry, Bloomberg reports. Russia's communications regulator, Roskomnadzor, listed Apple and Microsoft on October 2 as "organizers of information dissemination," a classification that carries obligations to preserve communications and make data available to Russian security agencies. Those obligations cover correspondence and messages containing audio or video. Companies must also keep information identifying users and recording the transmission of their communications within Russia for three years. items.snippet: The robot vacuums designed for large open floor plans often have big batteries but take up a ton of space. The SwitchBot K11+ Pro goes the other direction: a tiny vacuum, a small dock, and Matter support so it works with Apple Home. HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework. The SwitchBot K11+ Pro is 9.76 inches across and 3.62 inches tall, and weighs about 5 pounds. That size is the whole point. It can work its way between chair legs, get closer to corners and walls, and slide under beds, couches, and cabinets that larger robots bump into and give up on. If you have a couch that sits lower to the ground, you know what this means Navigation for the SwitchBot K11+ Pro is done by LiDAR for mapping and route planning, plus a close-range sensor for spotting furniture legs and following wall edges. items.title: Apple reveals pricing for Mac Studio with 512GB of RAM
items.snippet: When Apple announced the new M5 Max and M5 Ultra configurations of the Mac Studio in August, it said a configuration with 512GB of RAM would be available in October. Today, the company officially revealed the pricing of that option. If you head to the Mac Studio configurator on Apple’s website, you’ll see the new 512GB upgrade option. As previously announced, the 512GB option is only available with the top-tier M5 Ultra chip that has a 36-core CPU and 80‑core GPU. It’s a $15,500 upgrade over the base configuration of that processor, which has 96GB of unified memory. To put it another way: you’ll pay $22,299 for the Mac Studio with the top-tier M5 Ultra, 512GB of unified memory, and 1TB of storage. You can spec it up all the way to 16TB of storage, which brings the total price to $29,799.00. If you order a Mac Studio with 512GB of RAM, it’ll arrive in late November to early December. This is all thanks to a feature that has been a huge help whether I'm traveling longer distances or just heading out for groceries. items.title: iPhone Duo review: Proof that foldables don't have to suck
items.snippet: The iPhone Duo is far from perfect as a first-generation product, but it is a strong enough entry that will single-handedly lift foldables from passing fad to serious category for anyone. iPhone Duo review Apple has a habit of entering a market much later than its competitors then defining it . While it's too early to say if that's the case with iPhone Duo, it is clear that sometimes different can be enough to break the mold. Foldables first entered the market in 2019 as overpriced hunks of fragile plastic . While Android manufacturers have a better handle on build quality and feature sets in foldables seven years later, they still feel like incomplete experiments. Continue Reading on AppleI

items.title: The Only Good Easter Eggs Are Whole-Assed Easter Eggs
items.snippet: Marcin Wichary on the original iPod easter egg on Apple Music’s website 404 page: I am usually not a fan of easter eggs — most of them are poorly made — but this might be the best iPod recreation I’ve seen, and it’s an interesting thing to study: I think it generally covers all the modes etc. (with small exceptions) the typography looks accurate, it has the little “haptic” beeps, it has proper acceleration and the scrollbar, it has a little music library with various playlists, I have only noticed a few small bugs. items.title: Apple Drops App Store Commission by a Whopping 4 Percentage Points in Taiwan
items.snippet: Apple Developer News: Apple is making changes to the Taiwan storefront of the App Store, following discussions with the Taiwan Fair Trade Commission. As of October 31, 2026, the commission rate for standard Apple In-App Purchase and paid app transactions will be 26% on the Taiwan storefront of the App Store on iOS and iPadOS. Currently, that rate is 30%. Well there we go. The App Store in Taiwan — just like in Japan — is fixed. ★

items.title: KB5127936 finally fixes Windows 11 Always On VPN failures

items.title: Why AI hackers still fall for simple traps
